```{python}
#| label: load
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import openpyxl  # noqa: F401

xlsx = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scratch" / "uk_games_expo_2026_TomBrewstErr_own.xlsx"
    if "__file__" in globals()
    else Path("../scratch/uk_games_expo_2026_TomBrewstErr_own.xlsx")
)
df = pl.from_pandas(pd.read_excel(xlsx, engine="openpyxl"))
df = df.with_columns(pl.col("year_published").cast(pl.Int64, strict=False))
n_games = df.height

# Pre-compute the score range once so all badges across the report
# share the same color scale.
SCORE_MIN = float(df["mean_score"].min())
SCORE_MAX = float(df["mean_score"].max())
GEEK_MIN = float(df["predicted_geek_rating"].min()) if "predicted_geek_rating" in df.columns else 0.0
GEEK_MAX = float(df["predicted_geek_rating"].max()) if "predicted_geek_rating" in df.columns else 10.0


def bgg_link(game_id, name, year=None):
    yr_part = f" ({int(year)})" if year is not None and not pd.isna(year) else ""
    return (
        f'<a href="https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/{int(game_id)}" '
        f'target="_blank" rel="noopener">{name}{yr_part}</a>'
    )


def truncate(text, max_len=200):
    if not text or (isinstance(text, float) and pd.isna(text)):
        return ""
    text = str(text).replace("&#10;", " ").replace("\n", " ").strip()
    return text if len(text) <= max_len else text[: max_len - 3].rstrip() + "..."


def img_tag(url):
    if not url or (isinstance(url, float) and pd.isna(url)):
        return '<div class="thumb-empty"></div>'
    return f'<img src="{url}" class="thumb" />'


def score_badge(score, lo=SCORE_MIN, hi=SCORE_MAX, fmt="{:.3f}"):
    """Pill whose background blends from soft (lo) to accent (hi)."""
    s = float(score)
    rng = max(hi - lo, 1e-9)
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, (s - lo) / rng))
    return f'<span class="score-badge" style="--t:{t:.3f};">{fmt.format(s)}</span>'


def card_row(image_url, game_id, name, year, badges, description=None, rank=None):
    """Unified card used by every Predictions subsection.

    badges: list of (label, html_badge) tuples. The caller picks which
    scores to surface — LGBM/Logistic for Agreement/Disagreement,
    Tom Score/Geek Rating for Dark Horses/Skip.
    rank: optional 1-based position; rendered as a numbered chip on the
    left of the card.
    """
    yr = int(year) if year is not None and not pd.isna(year) else None
    link = bgg_link(game_id, name, yr)
    desc_html = (
        f'<div class="card-desc">{truncate(description)}</div>' if description else ""
    )
    badges_html = "".join(
        f'<span class="score-pair"><span class="score-label">{lbl}</span>{b}</span>'
        for lbl, b in badges
    )
    rank_html = f'<div class="card-rank">{rank}</div>' if rank is not None else ""
    return (
        '<div class="game-card">'
        f'{rank_html}'
        f'<div class="card-thumb">{img_tag(image_url)}</div>'
        '<div class="card-body">'
        f'<div class="card-title">{link}</div>'
        f'{desc_html}'
        f'<div class="card-scores">{badges_html}</div>'
        '</div></div>'
    )
```

Predictions come from two models trained on Tom's collection (LGBM and Logistic). The combined score below is the average of both. Higher = more likely Tom would own it.

## Top Games

Top 25 games most likely (average of both collection models) to fit Tom's collection.

```{python}
#| label: top25
from itables import show
import itables.options as opt
opt.lengthMenu = [10, 25]
opt.classes = "compact stripe hover"
opt.allow_html = True

top = df.head(25).to_pandas()
top25 = pd.DataFrame({
    "Rank": [f'<span class="rank-num">{i}</span>' for i in range(1, len(top) + 1)],
    "Image": [img_tag(u) for u in top.get("thumbnail", [None] * len(top))],
    "Game": [bgg_link(g, n, y) for g, n, y in zip(top["game_id"], top["name"], top["year_published"])],
    "Description": [truncate(d) for d in top.get("description", [""] * len(top))],
    "Tom Score": [score_badge(s) for s in top["mean_score"]],
})
show(
    top25,
    paging=True,
    pageLength=10,
    searching=False,
    ordering=False,
    scrollX=False,
    responsive=True,
    classes="compact stripe hover top-games-table",
    columnDefs=[
        {"targets": 0, "width": "60px", "className": "col-rank"},
        {"targets": 1, "width": "110px", "className": "col-thumb"},
        {"targets": 2, "width": "20%", "className": "col-game"},
        {"targets": 3, "className": "col-desc"},
        {"targets": 4, "width": "100px", "className": "col-score"},
    ],
)
```

## Predictions

Different views into how Tom's collection models and the BGG-universe models score these games.

### Model agreement

Top 10 games where both collection models agree most strongly. When the two models converge, the signal is stronger.

```{python}
#| label: agree
#| output: asis
m1, m2 = "lgbm_row_norm_v2", "logistic_row_norm_v2"
ranked = df.with_columns([
    pl.col(m1).rank(descending=True).alias("rk_lgbm"),
    pl.col(m2).rank(descending=True).alias("rk_logit"),
])
ranked = ranked.with_columns([
    ((pl.col("rk_lgbm") + pl.col("rk_logit")) / 2).alias("rk_avg"),
    (pl.col("rk_lgbm") - pl.col("rk_logit")).abs().alias("rk_disagreement"),
])
agree = ranked.sort("rk_avg").head(10)
print('<div class="game-card-list">')
for i, row in enumerate(agree.to_dicts(), 1):
    print(card_row(
        image_url=row.get("thumbnail"),
        game_id=row["game_id"],
        name=row["name"],
        year=row["year_published"],
        rank=i,
        badges=[
            ("LGBM", score_badge(row[m1])),
            ("Logistic", score_badge(row[m2])),
        ],
    ))
print('</div>')
```

### Model disagreement

Games in the top half overall where the two models disagree most about how to rank them. The most informative cases to look at — one model thinks they fit Tom's collection, the other doesn't.

```{python}
#| label: disagree
#| output: asis
fights = ranked.filter(pl.col("rk_avg") <= df.height * 0.5).sort("rk_disagreement", descending=True).head(8)
print('<div class="game-card-list">')
for i, row in enumerate(fights.to_dicts(), 1):
    print(card_row(
        image_url=row.get("thumbnail"),
        game_id=row["game_id"],
        name=row["name"],
        year=row["year_published"],
        rank=i,
        badges=[
            ("LGBM", score_badge(row[m1])),
            ("Logistic", score_badge(row[m2])),
        ],
    ))
print('</div>')
```

### Dark horses

Games Tom's collection model rates highly but the BGG-universe model expects to be poorly-received. Predicted as a fit for Tom even though the wider BGG audience isn't expected to rate them well.

```{python}
#| label: darkhorses
#| output: asis
score_col = "mean_score"
scored = df.with_columns([
    ((pl.col(score_col).rank() / df.height) - (pl.col("predicted_geek_rating").rank() / df.height)).alias("delta")
]).sort("delta", descending=True).head(8)
print('<div class="game-card-list">')
for i, row in enumerate(scored.to_dicts(), 1):
    s = row.get(score_col) or 0
    g = row.get("predicted_geek_rating") or 0
    print(card_row(
        image_url=row.get("thumbnail"),
        game_id=row["game_id"],
        name=row["name"],
        year=row["year_published"],
        rank=i,
        badges=[
            ("Tom Score", score_badge(s)),
            ("Geek Rating", score_badge(g, lo=GEEK_MIN, hi=GEEK_MAX, fmt="{:.2f}")),
        ],
    ))
print('</div>')
```

### Skip

Games the BGG-universe model expects to be well-received but Tom's collection model rates low. Likely hits with the wider audience that aren't predicted to fit Tom's collection.

```{python}
#| label: skip
#| output: asis
skipped = df.with_columns([
    ((pl.col("predicted_geek_rating").rank() / df.height) - (pl.col(score_col).rank() / df.height)).alias("delta")
]).sort("delta", descending=True).head(8)
print('<div class="game-card-list">')
for i, row in enumerate(skipped.to_dicts(), 1):
    s = row.get(score_col) or 0
    g = row.get("predicted_geek_rating") or 0
    print(card_row(
        image_url=row.get("thumbnail"),
        game_id=row["game_id"],
        name=row["name"],
        year=row["year_published"],
        rank=i,
        badges=[
            ("Tom Score", score_badge(s)),
            ("Geek Rating", score_badge(g, lo=GEEK_MIN, hi=GEEK_MAX, fmt="{:.2f}")),
        ],
    ))
print('</div>')
```

## All Games

Every scored game. **Tom: LGBM / Logistic** are P(Tom would own) from each collection model. **Predicted: Avg rating / Complexity / Geek rating** are from the production BGG-universe models — what the wider BGG audience is expected to say about each game.

```{python}
#| label: table
opt.lengthMenu = [10, 25, 50, 100]
opt.classes = "compact stripe hover"
opt.allow_html = True

full = df.to_pandas().copy()
full["Game"] = [bgg_link(g, n) for g, n in zip(full["game_id"], full["name"])]
full = full.rename(columns={
    "year_published": "Year",
    "lgbm_row_norm_v2": "Tom: LGBM",
    "logistic_row_norm_v2": "Tom: Logistic",
    "predicted_rating": "Predicted: Avg rating",
    "predicted_complexity": "Predicted: Complexity",
    "predicted_geek_rating": "Predicted: Geek rating",
})
full = full[[
    "Game", "Year",
    "Tom: LGBM", "Tom: Logistic",
    "Predicted: Avg rating", "Predicted: Complexity", "Predicted: Geek rating",
]]
show(full, paging=True, searching=True, scrollX=True, responsive=True)
```
